lead.headline: 0–4 after 120.4 to 153.6, and no claim tonight
lead.deck: Kamara's 22.8 on Monday made the score respectable and changed nothing. Three receivers still have no ruling. One coin flip to set in the flex.
lead.body: The week ended 120.4 to 153.6. Alvin Kamara scored twice from short range on Monday night and finished with 22.8, which lifted your total by 23 points and left you 33 short of Aye-Aye. On your bench Kyle Monangai's 28.0 and Ollie Gordon's 18.0 sat behind Bhayshul Tuten's 11.1; the best lineup you could have set scores 139.7, and that loses too. The bad news for Week 5 is that none of your three injured receivers has a ruling. Justin Jefferson's coach has 'no real projection', Terry McLaurin's promises an update on Wednesday, and Jalen Coker is on a bye and expected back afterwards. All three practise, or don't, after waivers process at 01:00 on Wednesday. So there is no claim tonight. Yesterday's brief said a Metcalf claim turned on Jefferson being ruled out, and he hasn't been. Metcalf would add less than a point to this week's lineup, and the seat he would take is Coker's, whom ESPN rates higher for the season. The lineup needs one change. The projection has Gordon in the flex over Kamara, 11.0 to 10.0. That is a coin flip, and coin flips go to the projection. Kamara played 38% of the snaps on Monday, shared third downs with a rookie and visited the medical tent. ESPN has you at 48% against Los Gigantes de Teca, whose best player, Ja'Marr Chase, is in the concussion protocol.

doFirst.headline: One coin flip in the flex; no claim
doFirst.deck: Gordon over Kamara, 11.0 to 10.0, on the projection. Everything else as set is the projection lineup.
doFirst.note: Set Gordon in the flex before Sunday at 11:00. No claim before waivers process at 01:00 Wednesday: Metcalf adds under a point this week and costs Coker, who is expected back in Week 6. Wednesday's practice reports on Jefferson and McLaurin are the next thing that can change the lineup.
doFirst.empty: One thing to set this Tuesday: Gordon in the flex over Kamara, a one-point coin flip that goes to the projection. No claim tonight.

roster.deck: As set you project 113.9 and the projection lineup is 114.9: the difference is Gordon over Kamara in the flex, a coin flip.

cannotSee.body: Kamara's 10.0 was published after his game. I can't see when ESPN last recomputed it, so 'priced' for Monday's news is an inference from the timestamp.

cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own, and the league file carries none. You are first of ten in this week's order. Everyone on the wire is on waivers until Wed 7 Oct at 01:00 Mexico City.

cannotSee.label: Matchup grades
cannotSee.body: Every tile comes from FootballDB's points allowed through Week 4, which is standard scoring and four games deep. DraftEdge, undated and full PPR, disagrees by ten places or more on Cleveland against receivers (27th or 15th) and Cincinnati against backs (11th or 25th). The Giants against receivers, for McLaurin, was not researched.

cannotSee.label: The wire screen
cannotSee.body: Keaton Mitchell, Antonio Williams, Oronde Gadsden and Tyler Higbee aren't on the published wire, so their availability in this league is the screen's inference that nobody rosters them.

cannotSee.label: Sources that disagree
cannotSee.body: Swift was benched (SI) or wasn't hurt and wasn't discussed (his coach). Monangai's imaging showed nothing structural by one summary that I could not confirm against its page. Kamara had 7 carries (four outlets and the archive) or 5 (AOL). Minnesota 'haven't scored a touchdown since Week 1' (Yahoo), which another box score contradicts. Dowdle's return is 'a pretty good chance' (Rapoport) and unconfirmed (McCarthy).

cannotSee.label: Reports I couldn't retrieve
cannotSee.body: ESPN pages returned empty, including its stories on Lamar Jackson, Kamara's knee and the Vikings' line. Hogs Haven, Bleeding Green Nation, Stampede Blue, Behind the Steel Curtain, Buffalo Rumblings, Acme Packing Company and the Star Tribune were blocked. RotoBaller gave navigation only and NBC Sports blurbs mostly a headline and one line. FantasyPros' and Sharp Football's defence-against-position tables did not render, so every matchup grade rests on FootballDB, which is standard scoring, with DraftEdge beside it. O'Connell's Monday press conference exists only as video. Pages were read through a summarising tool, so quotes are close but may not be exact.

cannotSee.label: The trade market
cannotSee.body: No trade this run. Three receivers have unknown timelines, and anything offered would be priced on guesses. The window the strategy names is Weeks 9 to 11.

cannotSee.body: Minnesota and Miami are both off in Week 6: Jefferson, Addison, the Vikings' defence and Gordon. That is next Tuesday's problem and the main reason Coker's Week 6 return matters.
